questions.prompt: At the endpoint of HCl + NaOH, what is in the flask?
10 mL of 0.2 mol/L NaOH neutralises 20 mL of HCl. What is the concentration of the HCl in mol/L?
Explain why an indicator is needed in a titration and how you know you have reached the endpoint.
questions.modelAnswer: Acid, alkali and salt solutions are usually colourless, so you can’t see when the acid has been exactly neutralised. An indicator changes colour at a certain pH. The endpoint is reached when the indicator just changes colour permanently (e.g. phenolphthalein turns faint pink) after adding one more drop while swirling.
rubric: Solutions colourless: need a visible sign
Permanent colour change after one drop
